note: Curated inputs for scripts/derive-costs.ts. Each figure is copied from the source named beside it. Rents per square metre and electricity prices are turned into monthly costs with the app assumptions below; other values are used as they are. Re-run the script after changing anything.

assumptions.description: App assumptions, not measured data: typical floor area and yearly household electricity use (not heating) by number of bedrooms.

dwelling.1: two-room flat (one bedroom and a living room)
dwelling.2: flat of three or more rooms
dwelling.3: flat of three or more rooms
dwelling.4: flat of three or more rooms

rent.limitations: Average rent per m² of new privately financed leases (Statistics Finland table 15fa); three-or-more-room flats share one figure. Heating is normally included; water and electricity are not.

waterPerPerson.basis: HSY water and wastewater fees for 2026 (€4.67 per m³ with VAT) at 130 litres a person a day; Motiva gives 90 to 270 litres, used for the range.
waterPerPerson.limitations: Landlords often bill water as a flat fee per resident, which can differ from metered cost.

transitPassAdult.basis: HSL 30-day season ticket, zones AB; the saver subscription costs €61.60.

healthcarePerPerson.basis: Household out-of-pocket health spending per inhabitant in Finland (€759.66 a year).
healthcarePerPerson.limitations: A national average across all ages; spending is lower for most working-age adults and higher for older people.

observation.basis: Municipal early-education fee from 1 August 2026: 10.7% of monthly gross household income above a threshold for the family size, at most €335 for the youngest child; under €32 nothing is charged. The second child pays 40% and each further child 20% of the youngest child's fee.
observation.limitations: Uses gross wage income only and counts children under 17 in the family size (the rule counts children under 18). Families of more than six use the threshold for six. Part-time care costs less.

dwelling.1: flat of any size (net cold rent)
dwelling.2: flat of any size (net cold rent)
dwelling.3: flat of any size (net cold rent)
dwelling.4: flat of any size (net cold rent)

rent.limitations: Median asking rent per m² across all advertised flats in Berlin (IBB Wohnungsmarktbericht 2025, 40,014 listings); no split by size. Net cold rent: operating costs and heating are added under utilities.

operatingCostsPerM2.basis: Operating costs billed to tenants in Germany, Betriebskostenspiegel for 2024 (Deutscher Mieterbund): the sum of all cost types, €3.31 per m² a month, including heating, hot water and water; €2.89 without lift, garden care and cable.

transitPassAdult.basis: Deutschlandticket, valid on all local transport in Germany; €66.80 from January 2027.

healthcarePerPerson.basis: Household out-of-pocket health spending per inhabitant in Germany (€702.63 a year).
healthcarePerPerson.limitations: A national average across all ages; spending is lower for most working-age adults and higher for older people.

childcarePerChild.basis: Kita places in Berlin are free; parents pay a €23 meal contribution. Providers may charge up to €100 more a month for extras.
childcarePerChild.limitations: Covers public and subsidised places; a place is not guaranteed at a particular Kita.

rent.limitations: Average asking rent per m² on idealista for the city of Madrid in September 2026; districts range from about €17 to €28.5. Existing leases are much lower (€12.8 per m² in 2022, Ministry of Housing reference index).

waterPerPerson.basis: Average water and sanitation cost in the Community of Madrid in 2024 (€1.74 per m³) at the measured average use of 128 litres a person a day (INE).

transitPassAdult.basis: 30-day public transport pass, zone A, at the 2026 discounted price (Consorcio Regional de Transportes, BOCM 31 Dec 2025).

healthcarePerPerson.basis: Household out-of-pocket health spending per inhabitant in Spain (€647.45 a year).
healthcarePerPerson.limitations: A national average across all ages; spending is lower for most working-age adults and higher for older people.

childcarePerChild.basis: Public nursery schools (0–3) in the Community of Madrid: tuition is free; meals cost €96 a month.
childcarePerChild.limitations: Public places are limited; private nurseries charge tuition, which is not included.

rentObservations.limitations: Not checked against HUD directly. Metro-wide rather than a specific neighbourhood; FY2027 differs. Verify a current listing before deciding.
rentObservations.basis: HUD FY2026 Fair Market Rent for the Austin metro, as republished by propmetrics.co: 40th percentile of gross rents paid by recent movers, including utilities except phone and internet.

transitPassAdult.basis: CapMetro calendar-month pass for local and rapid buses; fares rise on 10 January 2027.

healthcarePerPerson.basis: Employer health plan: the average worker share of a single-coverage premium ($1,440 a year, KFF 2025) plus out-of-pocket spending per person ($556.6 billion in 2024, CMS, over 340.0 million people).
healthcarePerPerson.limitations: Assumes employer coverage. Single premium is replaced by one family-plan premium for multi-person households. Actual plans and bad-year out-of-pocket costs can differ sharply; without employer coverage, marketplace premiums may be much higher.

childcarePerChild.basis: Average price of centre-based infant care in Texas ($11,349 a year; toddlers $10,921), Child Care Aware of America.
childcarePerChild.limitations: A Texas average; Austin prices are likely higher.

healthcareSinglePremiumMonthly.basis: KFF 2025 Employer Health Benefits Survey: worker contribution $1,440 a year for single employer coverage. This amount is already included in healthcarePerPerson.
healthcareSinglePremiumMonthly.limitations: Employer-plan average; the actual worker share varies by employer and plan.

healthcareFamilyPremiumMonthly.basis: KFF 2025 Employer Health Benefits Survey: worker contribution $6,850 a year for one family employer policy. Replaces the single premium for a household with two or more people.
healthcareFamilyPremiumMonthly.limitations: Employer-plan average; does not include out-of-pocket bills, which are added per person.

transitPassAdult.basis: Urban bus fare of 9 pesos (kept by Sonora's transport institute in August 2025) for 44 rides a month; 60 rides for the range. There is no monthly pass.
transitPassAdult.limitations: Assumes two rides a working day.

healthcarePerPerson.basis: Out-of-pocket health spending per person in Mexico (US$313.80 in 2023, World Bank) at the 2023 average exchange rate (17.74 pesos per dollar).
healthcarePerPerson.limitations: A national average. Salaried workers are covered by IMSS, but many people also pay for private care.

FI.basis: A new, non-luxury car in Finland: Todelliset Kulut (2026) puts an ordinary car at €600 to €900 a month; its example family car at about 15,000 km a year has depreciation of €250, insurance €80, fuel €180, maintenance and repairs €100, and tyres and wear €40 (its €300 loan payment is left out, because depreciation already counts the car's cost).
FI.runningBasis: What remains once the car is paid for: insurance €80, fuel €180, maintenance €100 and tyres €40 in Todelliset Kulut's example, about €400 a month; vehicle tax is not itemised.
FI.limitations: An unverified estimate from published articles, not a motoring association's study of this country; a national figure for about 15,000 km a year. To be checked before 1.0.

DE.basis: A new compact car such as a VW Golf at 15,000 km a year: ADAC's cost calculator gives €480 to €620 a month (as reported by fahrzeugschein.de, September 2026); mobile.de's Golf example gives €688 (depreciation €378, fuel €160, insurance and tax €93, workshop €57); carwow.de's Golf (July 2026) gives €529 without workshop costs or financing.
DE.runningBasis: What remains once the car is paid for (fuel, insurance, tax and workshop): €310 in mobile.de's example, and €228 plus workshop costs in carwow.de's, so about €260 to €310.
DE.limitations: An unverified estimate from published articles, partly from ADAC's calculator as reported by a third party; a national figure for about 15,000 km a year. To be checked before 1.0.

ES.basis: RACE (2026): keeping a petrol car costs €170 to €290 a month at 15,000 km a year, without depreciation; Motor16 gives €1,700 to €3,500 a year. Depreciation is added at 30 to 40% of the total, the share ADAC's figures give for Germany: about €354 a month (€243 to €483).
ES.runningBasis: What remains once the car is paid for: RACE's €170 to €290 a month for fuel, insurance, road tax, inspection and maintenance; €230 is the midpoint.
ES.limitations: An unverified estimate from published articles, with depreciation taken from German figures; a national figure for about 15,000 km a year. To be checked before 1.0.

PT.basis: Autocost user data, as reported by Caetano: keeping a car in Portugal costs about €328 a month (€3,939 a year), including depreciation.
PT.runningBasis: What remains once the car is paid for: the €328 less depreciation at 30 to 40% of the total, the share ADAC's figures give for Germany: about €213 (€197 to €230).
PT.limitations: An unverified single claim from user-entered data, not tied to a car size or mileage. To be checked before 1.0.

MX.basis: El Imparcial (9 October 2026): a financed compact car of 300,000 pesos costs 8,600 to 10,800 pesos a month: a 5,710-peso loan payment, 1,500 to 2,500 for petrol, 800 to 1,500 for comprehensive insurance, 400 to 700 for maintenance and 200 to 400 for state fees.
MX.runningBasis: What remains once the car is paid for: petrol, insurance, maintenance and state fees, 2,900 to 5,100 pesos a month in El Imparcial's example.
MX.limitations: An unverified single claim. The loan payment stands in for the cost of owning the car (it includes repaying it, not depreciation); parking, tolls and repairs are not included. To be checked before 1.0.

US.basis: AAA Your Driving Costs 2025: a new small sedan costs 55.87 cents a mile to own and run, $8,381 a year at 15,000 miles, including depreciation, finance charges, fuel, insurance, maintenance and fees.
US.runningBasis: What remains once the car is paid for: fuel, maintenance, insurance and fees make up 52.8% of AAA's average new-vehicle cost ($6,113 of $11,577), applied to the small sedan: about $369 a month.
US.limitations: A national average; insurance and fuel cost more in some states, including California. The running share is AAA's all-vehicle split applied to a small sedan.

CA.basis: WealthNorth (2026): a new mid-size sedan at $40,000 costs about $15,445 in its first year: depreciation $8,000, loan interest $1,470, insurance $2,100, fuel $2,475, maintenance $1,200 and licensing $200.
CA.runningBasis: What remains once the car is paid for: insurance, fuel, maintenance and licensing, $5,975 a year, about $498 a month. Ontario no longer charges for plate renewal.
CA.limitations: An unverified single claim for a mid-size sedan in its first year, when depreciation is highest; a compact car costs less. To be checked before 1.0.
